info.name: Building Connected APIs - Complete (v1.4.0)
info.description:
# Building Connected APIs — Complete Collection (v1.4.0)

A complete Postman collection for the **BuildingConnected & TradeTapp APIs**, generated from and
verified against every operation in the published API Reference:
https://aps.autodesk.com/en/docs/buildingconnected/v2/reference/http/

This collection supersedes `Building Connected APIs.postman_collection.json`, which is left unchanged.
It preserves that collection's folder structure, request names, request bodies and
`Authorization: Bearer {{Access_Token}}` header convention, and adds every remaining documented
operation, query parameter, request-body schema and response example.

## Authentication

Every operation requires a **three-legged (user context) access token**, obtained via the OAuth
Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. Each request sends:

```
Authorization: Bearer {{Access_Token}}
```

Set `Access_Token` in the `Building Connected Environment` environment. Required scopes are
`data:read` for read operations, `data:write` for create/update/delete, and `data:create` for
`POST /construction/tradetapp/v2/flags`. Requests that send a body also set
`Content-Type: application/json`.

## Base URLs

- `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/buildingconnected/v2`
- `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/buildingconnected/v3` (Projects and Project Team Members)
- `https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/tradetapp/v2`

## Pagination

List operations are cursor-paginated. Send `limit` (default 100; TradeTapp defaults to 20) and
`cursorState`. The response `pagination` object returns `limit`, `cursorState` and `nextUrl`;
when `cursorState` is absent there are no further pages. All documented `cursorState` parameters
are present on every list request in this collection (they were missing previously).

## Filtering syntax

- **Multi-value filters** — filters typed `array: string` accept a **comma-separated list**:
  `?filter[projectId]=id1,id2,id3`. Passing a single ID behaves exactly as before, so this is
  additive and not a breaking change. Applies to `filter[projectId]`, `filter[bidPackageId]`,
  `filter[state]`, `filter[action]`, `filter[bidderCompanyId]`, `filter[owningOfficeId]` and
  `filter[questionId]` on the operations that document them.
- **Date/time ranges** — `filter[updatedAt]` accepts a single ISO-8601 instant
  (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ`) or a range (`A..B`). Ranges may be open in either direction
  (`A..` or `..B`). The lower bound is inclusive, the upper bound exclusive.
- **`includeExternal`** — includes resources owned by external companies. It may only be combined
  with the specific filters listed on each operation (typically `filter[projectId]`,
  `filter[bidPackageId]`, `filter[userId]` or `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]`).
- All query parameters ship **disabled**; enable and fill only the ones you need.

## What is new in BuildingConnected API v1.4.0 (Public Beta release 2)

- **Bid Plugs API** — `Bids ▸ Plugs (New)` and `Bid Packages ▸ Bid Leveling (New)`.
- **Bid Highlights API** — `Bids ▸ Highlights (New)`.
- **Bid Notes API** — `Bids ▸ Notes (New)`.
- **Bid Leveling Settings API** — enable/disable plugs and highlights per bid package.
- **Other Cost Questions API** — up to 200 custom questions per bid package; `PUT` replaces the
  whole list rather than appending.
- **Other Cost Responses API** — structured per-bidder answers to those questions.
- **Bid Package Unsealing** — `Projects ▸ Sealed Bidding (New)`. One-way; only after the due date.
- **Clear ACC Docs folder association** — `currentAccDocsFolderId` can now be set to `null`
  independently of `currentAccLinkedProjectId` on `PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}`,
  `PATCH /v2/bid-packages:batch-patch` and `PATCH /v2/bid-packages/{bidPackageId}`.
- **Multi-value filtering** — comma-separated `filter[projectId]` / `filter[bidPackageId]` on
  bid-package activities, bid packages, bids, invites, invite notes and project team members (v2 and v3).
- **ACC-linked project visibility for bid forms** — `currentAccLinkedProjectId` is returned on both
  bid-form resources, and the list operations now accept `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` and
  `includeExternal`.

## Conventions

- Path parameters use Postman path variables (`:bidPackageId`) with empty values — fill them in
  the request's **Path Variables** table.
- Every request carries a description with the operation ID, endpoint, authentication context,
  required scopes, headers, path/query parameters, request-body schema and HTTP status codes.
- Every request carries a saved example response taken from the API Reference.
- Deprecated operations are grouped in `Deprecated (v2)` folders and labelled in their names.

request.description:
Retrieves a list of activities (history) of the bid packages that are associated with BuildingConnected projects owned by the requesting user’s company or projects the user is a team member of. At least one of the filters filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId], filter[projectId], filter[bidPackageId], or filter[inviteId] must be provided.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-bid-package-activities-GET`
**Endpoint:** `GET /construction/buildingconnected/v2/bid-package-activities`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:read`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…

**Query String Parameters**
- `cursorState` (string) — An opaque cursor token that identifies where the next page of paginated results should start. It’s returned in each paginated response so that it can be provided in the next request to continue paginated results. If a paginated response contains no cursorState value, there are no further pages to return. Omit this parameter to initiate a paginated request or to restart pagination.
- `limit` (int) — The maximum number of records that the endpoint may return per page. Note that a returned page may contain fewer records than the limit under either of these conditions: - There are fewer records found than the limit value. - The last page of a set is returned. Default value: 100
- `filter[projectId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The ID of a project with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[bidPackageId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The IDs of bid packages with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[inviteId]` (string) — The ID of an invite for which the bids returned in the response must have been submitted.
- `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` (string) — The ID of a Forma project with which the objects returned in the response are associated with BuildingConnected projects that are linked to this Forma Project.
- `filter[action]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — A comma separated list of actions. Only bid package activities with an action matching one in the list will be returned in the response.

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

item.name: Bid Packages

request.description:
Retrieves a list of the bid packages a user has access to. By default, only bid packages owned by the requesting user’s company are provided. This endpoint will additionally return bid packages on projects owned by other companies when the includeExternal parameter is provided. A bid package comprises a scope of work, and has several values that are independent from the project to which it belongs: date values, separate files options, and publication states. Invites are created for each bidder when a bid package is published or whenever a new bidder is added to a published bid package. These invites create corresponding opportunities on Bid Board Pro, and they inherit a combination of values from the bid package and the project.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-bid-packages-GET`
**Endpoint:** `GET /construction/buildingconnected/v2/bid-packages`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:read`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…

**Query String Parameters**
- `cursorState` (string) — An opaque cursor token that identifies where the next page of paginated results should start. It’s returned in each paginated response so that it can be provided in the next request to continue paginated results. If a paginated response contains no cursorState value, there are no further pages to return. Omit this parameter to initiate a paginated request or to restart pagination.
- `limit` (int) — The maximum number of records that the endpoint may return per page. Note that a returned page may contain fewer records than the limit under either of these conditions: - There are fewer records found than the limit value. - The last page of a set is returned. Default value: 100
- `filter[projectId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The ID of a project with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[updatedAt]` (string) — The required range of dates and times during which the last update must have been made to the objects returned in the response, in ISO 8601 format. A single date and time takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ, A date and time range takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ. Range queries can be closed or open in either direction: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.. or ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.
- `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` (string) — The ID of a Forma project with which the objects returned in the response are associated with BuildingConnected projects that are linked to this Forma Project.
- `filter[state]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — A comma separated list of states. Only bid packages with a state matching one in the list will be returned in the response.
- `includeExternal` (string) — Whether to include bid packages from external companies in the response. Possible values: true: External bid packages are included. false: (Default) External bid packages are not included. Note that this filter can be used only with filter[projectId] or filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId].

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Creates a bid package associated with a BuildingConnected project that is owned by the requesting user’s company. The requesting user must be a member of the project team. A bid package comprises a scope of work, and has several values that are independent of the project to which it belongs: date values, separate files options, and publication state. You can create the new bid package by specifying an existing (source) bid package as a template. Include the template object in the request to specify the types of content to copy from the source bid package. Note that any values you include in the request body take precedence over the corresponding values in the source bid package. A new bid package initially has the state field set to DRAFT. After a user performs the publishing operation in the BuildingConnected UI, the state field changes permanently to PUBLISHED. Note that you can add new bidders to the bid package in either state. An invite is created and sent to each existing bidder when the bid package is published, as well as when a new bidder is added to a published bid package. These invites create corresponding opportunities on Bid Board Pro, and they inherit a combination of values from the bid package and the project.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-bid-packages-POST`
**Endpoint:** `POST /construction/buildingconnected/v2/bid-packages`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Request Body**
- `projectId` (string) *(required)* — The ID of the project to which the bid package will belong. Max length: 24
- `name` (string) *(required)* — A user-defined name for the bid package, typically referring to a trade or scope of work such as “Concrete” or “Fire Alarms”. The name need not be unique. This value is listed as the trade on the bidder’s opportunity. This field is required and must…
- `number` (string) — A user-defined identifying number of the bid package. This value need not be unique.
- `keywords` (array: string) — An array of keywords to associate with the bid package. Keywords are used by the BuildingConnected search functionality to find relevant bidders for the bid package. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. A…
- `leadUserId` (string) — The unique BuildingConnected ID of the lead user for this bid package. All opportunities created from this bid package will appear to be sent from this user. If not provided, this defaults to the current user’s ID. Max length: 24
- `estimatedCost` (number) — A numeric value representing the expected contract cost for the bid package’s scope of work in the associated project’s defaultCurrency. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders.
- `instructions` (string) — The instructions for what to include in a bid for this bid package. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `bidsDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time by which bidders must submit their proposals for this bid package, in ISO 8601 format. Note that If a project has project.isBiddingSealed set to true, bids cannot be viewed before this date or submitted after this date. Note that…
- `endsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the scope of work of this bid package is expected to be completed, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this field and the useProjectEndsAt field are mutually exclusive. If endsAt is passed when useProjectEndsAt is true, the API will…
- `rfisDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time by which bidders must submit their RFIs for this bid package, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this field and the useProjectRfisDueAt field are mutually exclusive. If rfisDueAt is passed when useProjectRfisDueAt is true, the API will…
- `startsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the scope of work of this bid package is expected to start, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this field and the useProjectStartsAt field are mutually exclusive. If startsAt is passed when useProjectStartsAt is true, the API will…
- `jobWalkAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that bidders invited to this bid package may come to the site and do a job walk, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this field and the useProjectJobWalkAt field are mutually exclusive. If jobWalkAt is passed when useProjectJobWalkAt is…
- `currentAccDocsFolderId` (string) — The unique ID of an Autodesk Forma Data Management folder in the linked Forma project. Files in this folder are shared with the bid package’s bidders. The project to which the bid package belongs must be linked to a Forma project…
- `useProjectBidsDueAt` (boolean) — When set to true, indicates that the bidsDueAt on the Project level will be used for Bid Package bidsDueAt. Note that this field and the bidsDueAt field are mutually exclusive.
- `useProjectEndsAt` (boolean) — When set to true, indicates that the endsAt on the Project level will be used for Bid Package endsAt. Note that this field and the endsAt field are mutually exclusive.
- `useProjectJobWalkAt` (boolean) — When set to true, indicates that the jobWalkAt on the Project level will be used for Bid Package jobWalkAt. Note that this field and the jobWalkAt field are mutually exclusive.
- `useProjectRfisDueAt` (boolean) — When set to true, indicates that the rfisDueAt on the Project level will be used for Bid Package rfisDueAt. Note that this field and the rfisDueAt field are mutually exclusive.
- `useProjectStartsAt` (boolean) — When set to true, indicates that the startsAt on the Project level will be used for Bid Package startsAt. Note that this field and the startsAt field are mutually exclusive.
- `template` (object) — Information about an existing bid package from which this bid package will be copied.
  - `bidPackageId` (string) *(required)* — The ID of an existing (source) bid package from which this bid package will be copied. Max length: 24
  - `includeForm` (boolean) — Whether to copy the source bid package’s scope-specific bid form. Possible values: - true: (Default) The bid form is copied to the new bid package. - false: The bid form is not copied to the new bid package.
  - `includeFiles` (boolean) — Whether to copy the source bid package’s files. Possible values: - true: The files are copied to the new bid package. - false: (Default) The files are not copied to the new bid package.
  - `bidderStates` (array: string) — A list of the states of the source bid package’s invites to copy to the new bid package. Default value: [ ‘UNDECIDED’, ‘NOT_BIDDING’, ‘BIDDING’, ‘BID_SUBMITTED’, ‘NOT_INVITED’ ] Max 5 bidder states per bid package.

**HTTP Status Codes:** `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Creates multiple bid packages for provided projects The requesting user must be a member of the provided project’s team. A bid package comprises a scope of work, and has several values that are independent of the project to which it belongs: date values, separate files options, and publication state. Any of the new bid packages can be created by specifying an existing (source) bid package as a template. Include the template object in the request to specify the types of content to copy from the source bid package. Note that any values you include in the request body take precedence over the corresponding values in the source bid package. A new bid package initially has the state field set to DRAFT. After a user performs the publishing operation in the BuildingConnected UI, the state field changes permanently to PUBLISHED. Note that you can add new bidders to the bid package in either state. An invite is created and sent to each existing bidder when the bid package is published, as well as when a new bidder is added to a published bid package. These invites create corresponding opportunities on Bid Board Pro, and they inherit a combination of values from the bid package and the project. Max 100 bid packages per call.

item.name: Bids

request.description:
Retrieves a list of bids the requesting user has access to. By default, only bids received by the requesting user’s company will be returned. This endpoint will additionally return bids received on projects owned by external companies when the includeExternal parameter is provided. Bids are a combination of two sets of data: a proposal and levelled bid information. Proposals can be submitted by the project host or by a bidder. Bids can then be levelled on the BuildingConnected bid levelling tab. Plugs indicate the adjustments made by bid levelling. Bids have a many-to-one relationship with invites.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-bids-GET`
**Endpoint:** `GET /construction/buildingconnected/v2/bids`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:read`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…

**Query String Parameters**
- `cursorState` (string) — An opaque cursor token that identifies where the next page of paginated results should start. It’s returned in each paginated response so that it can be provided in the next request to continue paginated results. If a paginated response contains no cursorState value, there are no further pages to return. Omit this parameter to initiate a paginated request or to restart pagination.
- `limit` (int) — The maximum number of records that the endpoint may return per page. Note that a returned page may contain fewer records than the limit under either of these conditions: - There are fewer records found than the limit value. - The last page of a set is returned. Default value: 100
- `filter[projectId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The ID of a project with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[bidPackageId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The IDs of bid packages with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[inviteId]` (string) — The ID of an invite for which the bids returned in the response must have been submitted.
- `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` (string) — The ID of a Forma project with which the objects returned in the response are associated with BuildingConnected projects that are linked to this Forma Project.
- `filter[bidderCompanyId]` (string) — The BuildingConnected ID of a bidding company that must have submitted the bids that are returned in the response.
- `filter[updatedAt]` (string) — The required range of dates and times during which the last update must have been made to the objects returned in the response, in ISO 8601 format. A single date and time takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ, A date and time range takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ. Range queries can be closed or open in either direction: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.. or ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.
- `onlyLatestRevision` (boolean) — Whether to return only the latest revision of bids from an invited company. Possible values: - true: Only the latest revisions of bids are returned. - false: (Default) All revisions of bids are returned.
- `includeExternal` (boolean) — Whether to include bids from external companies in the response. Possible values: - true: External bids are included. - false: (Default) External bids are not included. Note that this filter can be used only with filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId] or filter[projectId] or filter[bidPackageId] or filter[inviteId].

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Creates a host bid (the value of creatorType is HOST). Any bid submitted by a member of the project team (or via the BuildingConnected API) on behalf of a bidder is a host bid. Note that bids cannot be updated; instead, you can use this endpoint to create a new bid that serves as a revision of an existing bid, based on the same inviteId. Only the latest revision is active. Note that the current version of the BuildingConnected API does not support adding plugs to bids. However, you can copy plugs from an old revision by passing a revision number to the applyPreviousPlugs parameter For more information about bids, see the Bids section of the BuildingConnected Field Guide. All required line items from the project and scope-specific bid forms must be present in the request. Each line item must either match a bid form line item or have isCustom set to true. A matching line item must have the same unique combination of type, description, section, code, and unit.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-bids-POST`
**Endpoint:** `POST /construction/buildingconnected/v2/bids`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Request Body**
- `inviteId` (string) *(required)* — The unique ID of the invite to which the bid applies. Max length: 24
- `notes` (string) — Information about the bid proposal.
- `total` (number) — A numeric value representing the total cost of the proposal not including any plugs, alternates, or other extra cost items. Combine this value with the project’s defaultCurrency to determine the monetary value of the proposal. Note that this field…
- `attachments` (array: string) — An array of the attachment IDs of the files to attach to the bid proposal. Note that an attachment ID is generated when you call POST bids/attachments to create the attachment. Note the value of id in the response. Max 50 attachments per bid.
- `lineItems` (array: object) — An array of the line item objects that will comprise the bid. All required line items from the project and scope-specific bid forms must be present in the request. Each line item must either match a bid form line item or have isCustom set to true. A…
  - `type` (enum:string) *(required)* — The line item’s type. The possible values have the following UI equivalents: - ACKNOWLEDGMENT — General Acknowledgments - ADDENDUM — Scope-Specific Information and Unit Costs - ALTERNATE — Alternates - BONDING — Bond Information - CERTIFICATION —…
  - `description` (string) *(required)* — A description of the line item.
  - `section` (string) — The bid section that the line item is under. This value is null if the item is not under a section. The section must match on the bid form.
  - `isCustom` (boolean) — Indicates whether the line item is a custom item added by the bidder instead of being on the bid form. Possible values: - true: The item is being added by the bidder. - false: The item matches a line item on the bid form. A custom line item must…
  - `unit` (enum:string) — The unit format of the line item. Custom line items (line items that are not on the bid form) have a limited set of possible types, each with a single corresponding unit format. Use the value TOTAL_COST_ONLY for a lump sum line item. The possible…
  - `code` (string) — A code associated with the line item on the bid form.
  - `quantity` (number) — The quantity of the line item. Note that this field is relevant only under both of the following conditions (otherwise it is converted to null): - The value of type is ALTERNATE or COST_BREAKDOWN. - The value of unit is neither TEXT nor…
  - `unitCost` (number) — The cost per unit of the line item. This is not the total cost of the line item. Note that this field is relevant only under both of the following conditions (otherwise it is converted to null): - The value of type is ALTERNATE or COST_BREAKDOWN. -…
  - `value` (one of) — The total value of the line item. Note the following requirements: - If type is SCOPE_CLARIFICATION or DISCLAIMER, this field is not relevant. - If unit is TEXT, YES_NO, or YES_NO_WITH_ADJUSTMENT, this field is a string. Otherwise, it is a number. -…
    - `0` (string) — The value as a text string. Used when unit is TEXT, YES_NO, or YES_NO_WITH_ADJUSTMENT.
    - `1` (number) — The value as a number. Used for all other unit types.
- `applyPreviousPlugs` (number) — The revision number from which you want to copy plugs. Set to -1 to copy plugs from the latest revision. Note that the first bid has a revision number of 0 (zero)

**HTTP Status Codes:** `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Retrieves a list of bid package invites the requesting user has access to. By default, only invites sent by the requesting user’s company will be returned. This endpoint will additionally return invites on projects owned by external companies when the includeExternal parameter is provided. An invite represents a solicitation sent to a potential bidder to bid on a bid package. Invites may include individuals from multiple companies, but the invite is “owned” by one company. Invites create opportunities on the bidder’s Bid Board when the bid package is published. A company invited on multiple bid packages will recieve multiple invites.

request.description:
Retrieves a list of invite notes. These notes are internal memos for tracking the progress of the invite. At least one of the filters filter[projectId] or filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId] must be provided. This endpoint will additionally return invite notes on projects owned by external companies when the includeExternal parameter is provided

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-invites-notes-GET`
**Endpoint:** `GET /construction/buildingconnected/v2/invite-notes`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:read`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…

**Query String Parameters**
- `cursorState` (string) — An opaque cursor token that identifies where the next page of paginated results should start. It’s returned in each paginated response so that it can be provided in the next request to continue paginated results. If a paginated response contains no cursorState value, there are no further pages to return. Omit this parameter to initiate a paginated request or to restart pagination.
- `limit` (int) — The maximum number of records that the endpoint may return per page. Note that a returned page may contain fewer records than the limit under either of these conditions: - There are fewer records found than the limit value. - The last page of a set is returned. Default value: 100
- `filter[projectId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The ID of a project with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[bidPackageId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — The IDs of bid packages with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `filter[inviteId]` (string) — The ID of an invite for which the bids returned in the response must have been submitted.
- `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` (string) — The ID of a Forma project with which the objects returned in the response are associated with BuildingConnected projects that are linked to this Forma Project.
- `filter[bidderCompanyId]` (string) — The ID of a bidder company with which the objects returned in the response must be associated.
- `includeExternal` (boolean) — Whether to include invite notes from external companies in the response. Possible values: true: External invite notes are included. false: (Default) External invite notes are not included. Note that this filter can be used only with filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId] or filter[projectId].

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Creates a new opportunity-project pair to relink a project from a group child opportunity to its group parent. When you use POST projects to create a project from an opportunity, it also links the project with the opportunity as a pair. The paired opportunity might later be grouped under a new group parent opportunity (see the Create and Manage Opportunities tutorial.) The project remains paired with that now-child opportunity. Use this endpoint to remove that pair link and relink the project to the new group parent. Note that this endpoint cannot be used to link an unlinked project to an opportunity. Example scenario: - There are 2 opportunities: Opp1 and Opp2. - Opp1 and Opp2 are grouped under parent opportunity GroupA. - Project Prj1 is linked to Opp1. Use POST opportunity-project-pairs to relink Prj1 to GroupA. Prj1 is no longer linked to Opp1. For more information about opportunity-project pairs, see the Manage Opportunity Projects and Pairs tutorial.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-opportunity-project-pairs-POST`
**Endpoint:** `POST /construction/buildingconnected/v2/opportunity-project-pairs`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Request Body**
- `opportunityId` (string) — The ID of a group parent opportunity to which the project identified by projectId should be linked. Note that this endpoint can be used only to re-link a project from one of the group parent’s children. Max length: 24
- `projectId` (string) — The ID of the project to re-link from a child opportunity to the parent opportunity identified by opportunityId. Max length: 24

**HTTP Status Codes:** `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Relinks a project from an opportunity group child that it’s paired with to the group parent. The link between the project and the child opportunity is removed. This endpoint can be used only when the existing opportunity-project pair has a value of true for the shouldRelinkGroup field. This happens when a new child opportunity linked to a project is added to a group already linked to a project, as shown in the following scenario. Example scenario: - There are 3 opportunities: Opp1, Opp2, and Opp3. - Opp1 and Opp2 are grouped under parent opportunity GroupA. - Project Prj1 is linked to GroupA. - Project Prj2 is linked to Opp3. - You add Opp3 to GroupA. Use PATCH opportunity-project-pairs to relink Prj2 with GroupA. Prj2 is no longer linked to Opp3, and Prj1 is no longer linked to GroupA. For more information about opportunity-project pairs, see the Manage Opportunity Projects and Pairs tutorial.

request.description:
Manually creates a new opportunity in BidBoard. Opportunities created using the BuildingConnected API have a source field value of API.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-opportunities-POST`
**Endpoint:** `POST /construction/buildingconnected/v2/opportunities`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Request Body**
- `name` (string) *(required)* — The name of the project, such as “Salesforce Tower” or “Chase Center”, that this opportunity will be part of. The name need not be unique. The name is required and must not be empty.
- `number` (string) — A user-defined identifying number for the opportunity. This value need not be unique.
- `client` (object) — Information about the client company issuing the bid opportunity.
  - `lead` (one of) — The lead contact at the client’s company.
    - `0` (object) — Lead contact by user ID.
      - `id` (string) *(required)* — The BuildingConnected user ID of the client’s lead contact. Max length: 24
    - `1` (object) — Lead contact by email.
      - `email` (string) *(required)* — The email address of the client’s lead contact.
  - `office` (object) — The client company’s office that is issuing the bid opportunity.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The office ID of the office issuing the opportunity. Max length: 24
- `customTags` (array: string) — An array of user-defined string values that characterize the opportunity. Max 60 tags per opportunity.
- `requestType` (enum:string) — The type of the opportunity. Possible values: PROPOSAL, BUDGET
- `submissionState` (enum:string) — The current state of the opportunity’s proposal. Default: UNDECIDED. Note that WILL_SUBMIT is equivalent to “accepted”. It is not possible to change the opportunity’s status to SUBMITTED. The API does not post bids on opportunities. Possible values:…
- `isParent` (boolean) — Indicates whether this opportunity is a group parent. Must be false if parentId is non-null. (An opportunity cannot be both group parent and group child.) Note that a group parent can be empty until child opportunities are added to the groupChildren…
- `parentId` (string) — The ID of this opportunity’s group parent opportunity, indicating that this is a group child. If this field is non-null, isParent must be false. (If this opportunity has a group parent, it cannot also be a group parent.) The identified parent…
- `groupChildren` (array: string) — An array of the unique IDs of group child opportunities that are grouped under this parent opportunity. This array is relevant only if isParent is set to true. Max 50 children per opportunity.
- `members` (array: object) — An array of the users following this opportunity. Note that only one member may have a type value of ASSIGNEE. Max 40 members per opportunity.
  - `userId` (string) — The unique BuildingConnected user ID of an opportunity member. Max length: 24
  - `type` (enum:string) — The opportunity member’s relationship to the opportunity (for improved indexing and queries). Note that the value ASSIGNEE may be set for only one member. Possible values: ASSIGNEE, FOLLOWER, VENDOR
- `dueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that bids must be submitted for the opportunity, in ISO 8601 format.
- `jobWalkAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that a job walk for the opportunity is scheduled, in ISO 8601 format.
- `rfisDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that pre-bid RFIs are due, in ISO 8601 format.
- `expectedStartAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected date and time that construction will start on site, in ISO 8601 format.
- `expectedFinishAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected date and time that the construction project or a specified scope of work covered by the opportunity will complete, in ISO 8601 format.
- `invitedAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the invite corresponding to this opportunity was received, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this value is not the same as createdAt, to account for an invite that may have been received before the opportunity was created in Bid…
- `tradeName` (string) — A user-defined name for the trade to which the opportunity applies.
- `projectSize` (number) — The area of the project in square feet. Note that this value is always returned in units of square feet regardless of the unit it was originally specified with. For example, if it was specified in square meters, it will be converted to square feet.
- `projectInformation` (string) — General information about the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `location` (one of) — The details to set or update a location.
  - `0` (object) — The structured address details to set or update a location.
    - `country` (string) — The country code of the location.
    - `state` (string) — The state, territory, or province code of the location.
    - `streetName` (string) — The street name of the location. This can be combined with streetNumber to get the street address.
    - `streetNumber` (string) — The numeric value of the street address. This can be combined with streetName to get the street address.
    - `suite` (string) — The suite number or second address line of the location.
    - `city` (string) — The city of the location.
    - `zip` (string) — The ZIP or Postal code of the location.
  - `1` (object) — The complete address to find.
    - `complete` (string) *(required)* — The complete address to validate.
- `tradeSpecificInstructions` (string) — Description provided for the specific scope of work requested in the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `architect` (string) — The name of the architect associated with the opportunity.
- `engineer` (string) — The name of the project engineer associated with the opportunity.
- `propertyOwner` (string) — The name of the property owner associated with the opportunity.
- `propertyTenant` (string) — The name of the property tenant associated with the opportunity.
- `declineReasons` (array: string) — The user’s internal justification for declining to bid on the opportunity. This can be set only if the value of submissionState is DECLINED. Max 11 decline reasons per opportunity.
- `additionalInfo` (string) — Internal notes on the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `priority` (enum:string) — The priority of this opportunity relative to other opportunities in your pipeline. Possible values: - LOW - MEDIUM - HIGH - UNKNOWN (Default)
- `marketSector` (enum:string) — An internal value indicating the market sector of the construction project for tracking purposes. Possible values: NONE, AIRPORT, ASSISTED_LIVING, AUTOMOTIVE_SERVICE_STATION, BRIDGE_TUNNEL, CASINO_GAMING, CLUBHOUSE, CONVENTION_CENTER, DATA_CENTER,…
- `rom` (number) — The bidder company’s rough order of magnitude estimate of the value of the opportunity, provided as a number. Use the value of the opportunity’s defaultCurrency field to calculate the monetary value.
- `winProbability` (number) — A numeric value representing your company’s best guess at your probability of winning this opportunity. A value of 90 represents a high probability. Possible values: 10, 30, 50, 70, 90, and null.
- `followUpAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the assignee should follow up on the opportunity, in ISO 8601 format. Bid Board will send the assignee a reminder email on this date.
- `contractStartAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that you expect the contract to start, in ISO 8601 format. Bid Board will send the assignee a reminder email on this date.
- `contractDuration` (number) — The number of weeks you expect the contract to last.
- `averageCrewSize` (number) — The average number of crew members you expect to be required on site during the contract.
- `estimatingHours` (number) — The number of hours that you expect to take to estimate the contract work for the opportunity.
- `feePercentage` (number) — The percentage of fees a subcontractor can track for the opportunity.
- `profitMargin` (number) — The percent margin of profit that a subcontractor can track for the opportunity.
- `finalValue` (number) — The final proposed value of the user’s bid for this opportunity. Often times a subcontractor will negotiate after a bid has been submitted, and the price you submitted may not be the final price. This field is used to indicate that final proposal…
- `owningOfficeId` (string) — The unique ID of the BuildingConnected office to which this opportunity belongs. If not provided, this defaults to the API user’s primary office ID. Max length: 24

**HTTP Status Codes:** `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-opportunities-opportunityId-GET`
**Endpoint:** `GET /construction/buildingconnected/v2/opportunities/{opportunityId}`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:read`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…

**Path Parameters**
- `opportunityId` (string) — The ID of the opportunity. To find the opportunity ID, call GET opportunities

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

request.description:
Updates the specified opportunity. You can update fields such as the project name, status, bid due date, client information, and linked project.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-opportunities-opportunityId-PATCH`
**Endpoint:** `PATCH /construction/buildingconnected/v2/opportunities/{opportunityId}`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Path Parameters**
- `opportunityId` (string) — The ID of the opportunity. To find the opportunity ID, call GET opportunities

**Request Body**
- `name` (string) — The name of the project, such as “Salesforce Tower” or “Chase Center”, that this opportunity will be part of. The name need not be unique. The name is required and must not be empty.
- `number` (string) — A user-defined identifying number for the opportunity. This value need not be unique.
- `client` (object) — Information about the client company issuing the bid opportunity.
  - `lead` (one of) — The lead contact at the client’s company.
    - `0` (object) — The lead contact by ID.
      - `id` (string) *(required)* — The BuildingConnected user ID of the client’s lead contact. Max length: 24
    - `1` (object) — The lead contact by email.
      - `email` (string) *(required)* — The email address of the client’s lead contact.
  - `office` (object) — The client company’s office that is issuing the bid opportunity.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The office ID of the office issuing the opportunity. Max length: 24
- `customTags` (array: string) — An array of user-defined string values associated with the opportunity. Max 60 tags per opportunity.
- `requestType` (enum:string) — The type of the opportunity. Possible values: PROPOSAL, BUDGET
- `submissionState` (enum:string) — The current state of the opportunity’s proposal. Default: UNDECIDED. Note that WILL_SUBMIT is equivalent to “accepted”. Possible values: UNDECIDED, WILL_SUBMIT, DECLINED
- `parentId` (string) — The ID of this opportunity’s group parent opportunity, indicating that this is a group child. The identified parent opportunity must have its isParent field set to true. Note that if this opportunity is a group parent (the isParent field is set to…
- `groupChildren` (array: string) — An array of the unique IDs of group child opportunities that are grouped under this opportunity. Note that this array is relevant only if this is a parent opportunity (the isParent field is set to true). You cannot modify the value of isParent. If…
- `members` (array: object) — An array of the users following the opportunity. Note that only one member may have a type value of ASSIGNEE. Max 40 members per opportunity.
  - `userId` (string) — The unique BuildingConnected user ID of an opportunity member. Max length: 24
  - `type` (enum:string) — The opportunity member’s relationship to the opportunity (for improved indexing and queries). Note that the value ASSIGNEE may be set for only one member. Possible values: ASSIGNEE, FOLLOWER, VENDOR
- `dueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that bids must be submitted for the opportunity, in ISO 8601 format.
- `jobWalkAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that a job walk for the opportunity is scheduled, in ISO 8601 format.
- `rfisDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that pre-bid RFIs are due, in ISO 8601 format.
- `expectedStartAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected date and time that construction will start on site, in ISO 8601 format.
- `expectedFinishAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected date and time that the construction project or a specified scope of work covered by the opportunity will complete, in ISO 8601 format.
- `invitedAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the invite corresponding to this opportunity was received, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this value is not the same as createdAt, to account for an invite that may have been received before the opportunity was created in Bid…
- `tradeName` (string) — A user-defined name for the trade to which the opportunity applies.
- `projectSize` (number) — The area of the project in square feet. Note that this value is always returned in units of square feet regardless of the unit it was originally specified with. For example, if it was specified in square meters, it will be converted to square feet.
- `projectInformation` (string) — General information about the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `location` (one of) — The details to set or update a location.
  - `0` (object) — The structured address details to set or update a location.
    - `country` (string) — The country code of the location.
    - `state` (string) — The state, territory, or province code of the location.
    - `streetName` (string) — The street name of the location. This can be combined with streetNumber to get the street address.
    - `streetNumber` (string) — The numeric value of the street address. This can be combined with streetName to get the street address.
    - `suite` (string) — The suite number or second address line of the location.
    - `city` (string) — The city of the location.
    - `zip` (string) — The ZIP or Postal code of the location.
  - `1` (object) — The complete address to find.
    - `complete` (string) *(required)* — The complete address to validate.
- `tradeSpecificInstructions` (string) — Description provided for the specific scope of work requested in the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `architect` (string) — The name of the architect associated with the opportunity.
- `engineer` (string) — The name of the project engineer associated with the opportunity.
- `propertyOwner` (string) — The name of the property owner associated with the opportunity.
- `propertyTenant` (string) — The name of the property tenant associated with the opportunity.
- `declineReasons` (array: string) — The user’s internal justification for declining to bid the opportunity. This can be set only if submissionState is DECLINED. Max 11 decline reasons per opportunity.
- `additionalInfo` (string) — Internal notes on the opportunity. This field may contain HTML tags for formatting.
- `priority` (enum:string) — The priority of this opportunity relative to other opportunities in your pipeline. Possible values: - LOW - MEDIUM - HIGH - UNKNOWN (Default)
- `marketSector` (enum:string) — An internal value indicating the market sector of the construction project for tracking purposes. Possible values: NONE, AIRPORT, ASSISTED_LIVING, AUTOMOTIVE_SERVICE_STATION, BRIDGE_TUNNEL, CASINO_GAMING, CLUBHOUSE, CONVENTION_CENTER, DATA_CENTER,…
- `rom` (number) — The bidder company’’s rough order of magnitude estimate of the value of the opportunity, provided as a number. Use the value of the opportunity’s defaultCurrency field to calculate monetary value.
- `winProbability` (number) — A numeric value representing your company’s best guess at your probability of winning this opportunity. A value of 90 represents a high probability. Possible values: 10, 30, 50, 70, 90, and null.
- `followUpAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that the assignee should follow up on the opportunity, in ISO 8601 format. Bid Board will send the assignee a reminder email on this date.
- `contractStartAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that you expect the contract to start, in ISO 8601 format. Bid Board will send the assignee a reminder email on this date.
- `contractDuration` (number) — The number of weeks you expect the contract to last.
- `averageCrewSize` (number) — The average number of crew members you expect to be required on site during the contract.
- `estimatingHours` (number) — The number of hours that you expect to take to estimate the contract work for the opportunity.
- `feePercentage` (number) — The percentage of fees a subcontractor can track for the opportunity.
- `profitMargin` (number) — The percent margin of profit that a subcontractor can track for the opportunity.
- `finalValue` (number) — The final proposed value of the user’s bid for this opportunity. Often times a subcontractor will negotiate after a bid has been submitted, and the price you submitted may not be the final price. This field is used to indicate that final proposal…
- `owningOfficeId` (string) — The unique ID of the BuildingConnected office to which this opportunity belongs. If not provided, this defaults to the API user’s primary office ID. Max length: 24

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`

Retrieves a list of the BuildingConnected projects a user has access to. By default, only projects owned by the requesting user’s company are provided. This endpoint will additionally return projects owned by other companies when the includeExternal parameter is provided. A BuildingConnected project represents a request for proposals, typically representing a single phase of bidding. It can be linked to a Forma project, but it’s technically separate, and may be related to the Forma project on a many-to-one basis. For example: a project may go through three phases of bidding before proceeding to site construction; this process could potentially be represented by three BuildingConnected projects and one Forma project. A project is a top-level container for all scopes of work in a phase of bidding. Each individual scope of work is presented as a bid package. Each bid package has bidders (represented by invites to bid), and each bidder creates bids in response to an invite.

If a paginated response contains no cursorState value, there are no further pages to return. Omit this parameter to initiate a paginated request or to restart pagination.
- `limit` (int) — The maximum number of records that the endpoint may return per page. Note that a returned page may contain fewer records than the limit under either of these conditions: - There are fewer records found than the limit value. - The last page of a set is returned. Default value: 100
- `filter[updatedAt]` (string) — The required range of dates and times during which the last update must have been made to the objects returned in the response, in ISO 8601 format. A single date and time takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ, A date and time range takes this format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ. Range queries can be closed or open in either direction: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.. or ..YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.SSSZ.
- `filter[owningOfficeId]` (array: string) **(accepts a comma-separated list of values)** — A comma separated list of office IDs that own the relevant objects. The owningOfficeId must belong to the requesting user’s company.
- `filter[userId]` (string) — The unique BuildingConnected user ID for which to query projects. Only projects this user has access to will be provided. Results will only include projects for which the requesting user also has access. The userId must belong to the requesting user’s company.
- `filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId]` (string) — The ID of a Forma project with which the objects returned in the response are associated with BuildingConnected projects that are linked to this Forma Project.
- `searchText` (string) — Search for projects whose name or number matches this text. It is case-insensitive and only matches from the start of a word.
- `includeClosed` (boolean) — Whether to include closed projects in the response. Possible values: - true: Closed projects are included. - false: (Default) Closed projects are not included.
- `includeExternal` (boolean) — Whether to include projects from external companies in the response. Possible values: - true: External projects are included. - false: (Default) External projects are not included. Note that this filter can be used only with filter[userId] or filter[currentAccLinkedProjectId].

request.description:
Creates a new BuildingConnected project in DRAFT state. The project can be created directly, or by cloning an existing project or copying information from an existing opportunity. When the project’s information is copied from another project or an opportunity, the values in the request body take precedence over the values in the originating project or opportunity.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-v3-projects-POST`
**Endpoint:** `POST /construction/buildingconnected/v3/projects`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Request Body**
- `name` (string) *(required)* — A user-defined name for the project such as “Salesforce Tower” or “Chase Center”. The name need not be unique. The name is required and must not be empty. Max length: 100
- `number` (string) — A user-defined value that will be prepended to name on invites sent to bidders. The value need not be unique. Max length: 100
- `client` (string) — A user-defined name for the client for whom the project is being bid. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 100
- `description` (string) — A detailed description of the project with HTML markup. Max length: 10000
- `notes` (string) — A free text field for miscellaneous notes, with HTML markup. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 4000
- `value` (number) — The monetary value of the project. Note that BuildingConnected projects do not have multi-currency support; all monetary values for a project, including bids, are assumed to be in the same currency. Note that this value is private to your company…
- `projectSize` (number) — The magnitude of the project, in the units that you specify in projectSizeUnits (SQUARE_FEET or SQUARE_METERS).
- `projectSizeUnits` (enum:string) — The unit type of the value of projectSize. Possible values: SQUARE_FEET, SQUARE_METERS
- `isBiddingSealed` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project’s bids are sealed. Sealed bids cannot be accessed until the due date is past, and new bids cannot be submitted if the due date is past. Possible values: - true: The project’s bids are sealed. - false: The project’s bids…
- `owningOfficeId` (string) — The owning office ID of the project. If omitted, this defaults to the API user’s primary office. Max length: 24
- `isPublic` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project should be listed in your company’s public plan room. Possible values: - true: The project is public. - false: The project is not public.
- `bidsDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which bidders must submit bids on this project, in ISO 8601 format. This field provides the default due date for the project’s bid packages, after which you can set an independent due date for each bid package.
- `endsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected end date and time of the project in ISO 8601 format. If startsAt is set and occurs after endsAt, the API will reject the request.
- `rfisDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which bidders must submit RFIs for this project, in ISO 8601 format.
- `startsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected start date and time of the project in ISO 8601 format.
- `jobWalkAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that bidders invited to this project may come to the site and do a job walk, in ISO 8601 format.
- `dueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which your bid must be submitted to the client, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders.
- `location` (one of) — The location of the project. Provide either structured address fields or a complete address string.
  - `0` (object) — The structured address details to set or update a location.
    - `country` (string) — The country code of the location.
    - `state` (string) — The state, territory, or province code of the location.
    - `streetName` (string) — The street name of the location. This can be combined with streetNumber to get the street address.
    - `streetNumber` (string) — The numeric value of the street address. This can be combined with streetName to get the street address.
    - `suite` (string) — The suite number or second address line of the location.
    - `city` (string) — The city of the location.
    - `zip` (string) — The ZIP or Postal code of the location.
  - `1` (object) — The complete address to find.
    - `complete` (string) *(required)* — The complete address to validate.
- `accountManager` (string) — The name of your company’s primary business contact responsible for communicating with the client owner of the project. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 100
- `feePercentage` (number) — A numeric value expressing the fee that your company will charge for the project. This value is a rational number that represents a percentage. For example, 15.55% is represented as 15.55. Note that this value is private to your company and is not…
- `marketSector` (string) — A description of the market sector that the project is in. Max length: 100
- `defaultCurrency` (enum:string) — The currency denomination used for the project. Possible values: - AUD: Australian dollar - CAD: Canadian dollar - EUR: Euro - GBP: British pound - USD: U.S. dollar - NZD: New Zealand dollar Note that future values will follow the ISO 4217 format…
- `architect` (string) — The name of the architect on the project. Max length: 100
- `isForBudgeting` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project is for budgeting rather than for bidding. Possible values: - true: The project is for creating budgeting requests. - false: The project is for creating bidding invites.
- `isCompetitive` (boolean) — Indicates whether this is a competitive or “hard bid” project rather than a negotiated project. Possible values: - true: The project is competitive. - false: The project is negotiated. This information is private to your company and is not shared…
- `currentAccLinkedProjectId` (string) — The project ID of a Forma project to link to with this project. Multiple BuildingConnected projects can be linked to one Forma project. The currentAccLinkedHubId field must also be provided. To obtain the hub and project IDs, see Retrieve Forma hub…
- `currentAccLinkedHubId` (string) — The ID of the hub where the Forma project specified by currentAccLinkedProjectId is located. Required if you include currentAccLinkedProjectId in the request. Multiple BuildingConnected projects can be linked to one Forma project. To obtain the hub…
- `currentAccDocsFolderId` (string) — The unique ID of an Autodesk Forma Data Management folder in the linked Forma project. Files in this folder are shared with all bidders in this bid package. The currentAccLinkedProjectId field must be specified to be able to set this value. Note…
- `relevantCertificates` (array: object) — An array of certificate attributes relevant to the project. This array is limited to a maximum of 50 certificates.
  - `agency` (object) — A certifying agency that’s relevant to this project.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The unique ID of a certification agency. Max length: 24
  - `certificateType` (object) — A type of certificate (issued by the specified agency) that’s relevant to this project.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The unique ID of a certificate type. Max length: 24
- `ndaId` (string) — The ID of the non-disclosure agreement (NDA) that members and bidders must sign to access the project. Set this field to null to remove the NDA requirement (for DRAFT projects only). Max length: 24
- `isProjectNameShownBeforeSigningNda` (boolean) — Indicates whether users who have not signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) can see the project name. Note that this field can be set only when one of the following is true, - when ndaId is passed - if you are linking the project with an…
- `originalProjectId` (string) — The unique ID of an original template or project from which this project will be cloned. Note that this field and the opportunityProjectPair object are mutually exclusive. Max length: 24
- `template` (object) — The elements from the original project to copy when originalProjectId is specified.
  - `includeInfo` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s information.
  - `includeCosts` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s costs.
  - `includeForm` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s bid form.
  - `includeFiles` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s files. If neither project is connected to Forma Data Management, the files are duplicated and recreated in the new project. When both the new project and the template project share currentACCLinkedProjectId…
  - `includeTeam` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s team. If the requesting user is not a member of the template’s team they will be added to the new project’s team.
  - `bidPackages` (object) — Information about bid packages and their properties to copy from the template project.
    - `includeForm` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original project’s scope-specific bid forms.
    - `includeFiles` (boolean) — Set to true to copy the original bid package’s files. If neither project is connected to Forma Data Management, the files are duplicated and recreated in the new bid package. When both the new project and the template project share…
    - `bidderStates` (array: string) — A list of the states of the invites that should be copied from the original project’s bid packages. Default: All states. Possible values: UNDECIDED, NOT_BIDDING, BIDDING, BID_SUBMITTED, and NOT_INVITED.
    - `ids` (array: string) — A list of the IDs of the bid packages to copy from the original project. Default: All bid packages.
- `opportunityProjectPair` (object) — Information about a BuildingConnected opportunity on which you want to base the new project. Note that this object and the originalProjectId field are mutually exclusive.
  - `opportunityId` (string) — The unique ID of the opportunity from which this project will be created. An opportunity-project pair will be created as a result. Max length: 24
  - `includeClientFiles` (boolean) — Whether to sync client files from the opportunity to the project. Possible values: - true: Client files from the opportunity are synced to the project. - false: (Default) Client files are not synced.
  - `includeInternalFiles` (boolean) — Whether to sync internal files from the opportunity to the project. Possible values: - true: Internal files from the opportunity are synced to the project. - false: (Default) Internal files are not synced.
  - `includeBidForm` (boolean) — Whether to copy the bid form from the opportunity to the project. Possible values: - true: The bid form is copied to the project. - false: (Default) The project has no bid form.
  - `includeNda` (boolean) — Whether to copy the NDA from the opportunity to the project. Possible values: - true: The NDA is copied to the project. The project will require signing the NDA. - false: (Default) The project has no NDA.

request.description:
Updates fields on the specified BuildingConnected project. You can update fields such as the project name, status, location, bid due date, and linked Forma project.

---

**Operation ID:** `buildingconnected-v3-projects-projectId-PATCH`
**Endpoint:** `PATCH /construction/buildingconnected/v3/projects/{projectId}`
**Authentication:** User context required
**Required OAuth Scopes:** `data:write`
**Data Format:** JSON

**Headers**
- `Authorization` *(required)* — Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow. The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified…
- `Content-Type` *(required)* — Must be application/json

**Path Parameters**
- `projectId` (string) — The ID of a BuildingConnected project.

**Request Body**
- `name` (string) — A user-defined name for the project such as “Salesforce Tower” or “Chase Center”. The name need not be unique. The name must not be empty if provided. Max length: 100
- `number` (string) — A user-defined value that will be prepended to name on invites sent to bidders. The value need not be unique. Max length: 100
- `client` (string) — A user-defined name for the client for whom the project is being bid. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 100
- `description` (string) — A detailed description of the project with HTML markup. Max length: 10000
- `notes` (string) — A free text field for miscellaneous notes, with HTML markup. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 4000
- `value` (number) — The monetary value of the project. Note that BuildingConnected projects do not have multi-currency support; all monetary values for a project, including bids, are assumed to be in the same currency. Note that this value is private to your company…
- `projectSize` (number) — The magnitude of the project, in the units that you specify in projectSizeUnits (SQUARE_FEET or SQUARE_METERS).
- `projectSizeUnits` (enum:string) — The unit type of the value of projectSize. Possible values: SQUARE_FEET, SQUARE_METERS
- `isBiddingSealed` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project’s bids are sealed. Sealed bids cannot be accessed until the due date is past, and new bids cannot be submitted if the due date is past. Possible values: - true: The project’s bids are sealed. - false: The project’s bids…
- `bidAdminUserId` (string) — The unique BuildingConnected ID of the user set as the “Bid Administrator” when project’s bids are sealed. Only the bid administrators can unseal bids after the bid’s due date. If the project is already sealed, only a current bid administrator can…
- `state` (enum:string) — The process state of the project. Use this field to transition the project between CLOSED and not CLOSED states. Possible values: - DRAFT: (Default) The project is unpublished. - PUBLISHED: One or more of the project’s bid packages has been…
- `ndaId` (string) — The ID of the non-disclosure agreement (NDA) that members and bidders must sign to access the project. ndaId cannot be updated on a published project. Set this field to null to remove the NDA requirement (for DRAFT projects only). Max length: 24
- `isProjectNameShownBeforeSigningNda` (boolean) — Indicates whether users who have not signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) can see the project name. Note that this field can be set only when one of the following is true, - when isNdaRequired is true - when ndaId is passed Possible values: -…
- `owningOfficeId` (string) — The owning office ID of the project. If omitted, this defaults to the API user’s primary office. Max length: 24
- `isPublic` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project is listed in your company’s public plan room. Possible values: - true: The project is public. - false: The project is not public.
- `bidsDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which bidders must submit bids on this project, in ISO 8601 format. This field provides the default due date for the project’s bid packages, after which you can set an independent due date for each bid package.
- `endsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected end date and time of the project in ISO 8601 format. If startsAt is set and occurs after endsAt, the API will reject the request.
- `rfisDueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which bidders must submit RFIs for this project, in ISO 8601 format.
- `startsAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The expected start date and time of the project in ISO 8601 format.
- `jobWalkAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time that bidders invited to this project may come to the site and do a job walk, in ISO 8601 format.
- `dueAt` (datetime: ISO 8601) — The date and time deadline by which your bid must be submitted to the client, in ISO 8601 format. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders.
- `location` (one of) — The location of the project. Provide either structured address fields or a complete address string.
  - `0` (object) — The structured address details to set or update a location.
    - `country` (string) — The country code of the location.
    - `state` (string) — The state, territory, or province code of the location.
    - `streetName` (string) — The street name of the location. This can be combined with streetNumber to get the street address.
    - `streetNumber` (string) — The numeric value of the street address. This can be combined with streetName to get the street address.
    - `suite` (string) — The suite number or second address line of the location.
    - `city` (string) — The city of the location.
    - `zip` (string) — The ZIP or Postal code of the location.
  - `1` (object) — The complete address to find.
    - `complete` (string) *(required)* — The complete address to validate.
- `accountManager` (string) — The name of your company’s primary business contact responsible for communicating with the client owner of the project. Note that this value is private to your company and is not displayed to bidders. Max length: 100
- `feePercentage` (number) — A numeric value expressing the fee that your company will charge for the project. This value is a rational number that represents a percentage. For example, 15.55% is represented as 15.55. Note that this value is private to your company and is not…
- `marketSector` (string) — A description of the market sector that the project is in. Max length: 100
- `defaultCurrency` (enum:string) — The currency denomination used for the project. Possible values: - AUD: Australian dollar - CAD: Canadian dollar - EUR: Euro - GBP: British pound - USD: U.S. dollar - NZD: New Zealand dollar Note that future values will follow the ISO 4217 format…
- `architect` (string) — The name of the architect on the project. Max length: 100
- `isForBudgeting` (boolean) — Indicates whether the project is for budgeting rather than for bidding. Possible values: - true: The project is for creating budgeting requests. - false: The project is for creating bidding invites.
- `isCompetitive` (boolean) — Indicates whether this is a competitive or “hard bid” project rather than a negotiated project. Possible values: - true: The project is competitive. - false: The project is negotiated. This information is private to your company and not shared with…
- `currentAccLinkedProjectId` (string) — The project ID of the Forma project to link with this project. Multiple BuildingConnected projects can be linked to one Forma project. Note that the currentAccLinkedHubId field must be provided unless it is already set to the expected value. To…
- `currentAccLinkedHubId` (string) — The ID of the hub where the Forma project specified by currentAccLinkedProjectId is located. Required if you include currentAccLinkedProjectId in the request. Multiple BuildingConnected projects can be linked to one Forma project. To obtain the hub…
- `currentAccDocsFolderId` (string) — The unique ID of an Autodesk Forma Data Management folder in the linked Forma project. Files in this folder are shared with all bidders. The currentAccLinkedProjectId field must be specified to be able to set this value. Note that if you provide a…
- `relevantCertificates` (array: object) — An array of certificate attributes relevant to the project. The array is limited to a maximum of 50 certificates.
  - `agency` (object) — A certifying agency that’s relevant to this project.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The unique ID of a certification agency. Max length: 24
  - `certificateType` (object) — A type of certificate (issued by the specified agency) that’s relevant to this project.
    - `id` (string) *(required)* — The unique ID of a certificate type. Max length: 24
- `outcome` (object) — Outcome of the closed project. Can only be set on a non-budgeting and competitive project when project.state is CLOSED. All values are null by default except outcome.awarded, which defaults to UNKNOWN.
  - `awarded` (object) *(required)* — Outcome of this Project. Possible values: - WON: Indicates that user’s company won this job. - LOST: Indicates that user’s company lost this job. - UNKNOWN: Indicates some other outcome for this project, e.g., the project went to rebid. Default is…
  - `notifyBidders` (boolean) — Indicates whether bidders who submitted through BuildingConnected should be notified when the project is lost and closed. Note that this value can be set only when project.state is CLOSED and outcome.awarded is LOST.
  - `notificationMessage` (string) — The message to send to bidders who submitted through BuildingConnected when the project is lost and closed. Note that this value can be set only when notifyBidders is true. Max length: 5242880

**HTTP Status Codes:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `429`, `500`
